marks.q: Adjusted PBT for the Group increased by 70%, with strong growth across all businesses. It is expected that the Group will continue to grow in the second half.

However, as a direct result of the wholesale gas price increases impacting Q4 and subsequently, the profitability of the Paper division, our expectations for the full year will be for adjusted* PBT for the Group of £3.5M (FY2021: £1.1M) against previous market expectations of adjusted* PBT of £4.9M.
Looking forward, the outlook remains positive across the Group as we enter the new financial year with a record order book.
Profits for the group are currently tracking ahead of plan and significantly ahead of the prior-year quarter, with management expectations for FY23 presently unchanged.
marks.gnote: early signal: first step up in tone

marks.q: As a result of the current unprecedented macro-economic environment, management expectations for FY23 have been reduced with a year-end adjusted PBT of £2.0m against previous market expectations of adjusted PBT of £5.4m.

Taking into consideration the current unprecedented macro‐economic environment and the cost mitigation actions put in place, management expectations for the FY23 have been reduced with a year‐end adjusted PBT of £2.0m against previous market expectations of adjusted PBT of £5.4m.
The Company, subject to audit, expects to generate £130 million revenue for FY23 and an adjusted profit before tax of not less than £2.2 million, exceeding market expectations of £2.0 million.

Adjusted profit before tax (see APM 2 Alternative Performance Measures) was £3,195k in the year and ahead of market expectations, partly due to stronger trading in TFP and the accounting adjustments of provisions relating to TFP.

The Group's start to the financial year has seen revenue broadly in line with the Board's expectations, with strong gross margins and improvement in the cost landscape leading to operating profit in line with expectations.

The actions taken to date give the Board confidence that the Group is well positioned to deliver increased profitability in FY24 consistent with its expectations and that, in line with the accelerated growth strategy, revenue growth will be delivered from FY25 onwards.
FY2024 adjusted PBT is expected to be materially below prior management expectations, with the Board now expecting to report a small adjusted profit before tax for the year.
For FY2024, the Board expects, subject to audit, to report revenue in line with, and profits slightly ahead of its previous expectations.
FY2025 year-to-date trading has been in line with the Board's expectations.
Trading is in line with the Board's expectations, albeit behind the performance seen over the same period last year where Advanced Materials fuel cell revenue was particularly strong.

As a result of the prolonged weakness in Paper & Packaging market conditions, the Board now expects that the Group's results for FY25 will be below its prior expectations, with full year revenue and adjusted1 profit before tax expected to be broadly at the same level as the Group's FY24 reported results.
Adjusted EBITDA consistent with the Board's expectations and the prior financial period ended 30 March 2024 ("FY24");
Overall, the Board is confident that the Group will deliver significant growth in Adjusted EBITDA profitability in FY26 against FY25.

For FY26, the Board expects to see the initial results from the implementation of the new strategy and is confident that the Group will deliver significant growth in Adjusted EBITDA profitability against FY25.

Performance in the Period has been slightly ahead of expectations in both divisions with good progress in the execution of the Board's updated strategy, outlined at the Capital Markets Event on 18 June 2025.

The Board remains focused on disciplined strategic execution with full-year revenues anticipated at similar levels to FY25.  Full-year expectations for Adjusted EBITDA are unchanged, with significant growth versus the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA1 of £8.8m, approximately 10% ahead of market expectations and more than 30% ahead of the prior year (FY25: £6.67m):
Trading momentum into FY27 has been positive with a strong start in the first quarter underpinning the Board's expectations for the full year.
The Board expects full year trading to be in line with market expectations.

As a result of the performance delivered in the first half, together with the Board's current assessment of the outlook for the remainder of the financial year ending 27 March 2027, the Board now expects full-year Adjusted EBITDA to be approximately 10% to 20% ahead of current market expectations of £9.4 million.
